5.PRICING What the money buys Typical small jobs: USD 100 to 500, fixed price, agreed before work starts. The examples below are scopes taken from quotes we wrote in October 2026. They are not finished jobs and they are not a menu; they show the size of work each amount usually covers. Every price is agreed in writing before anything starts. Price What it typically buys What is included USD 100 A small command-line tool: read an Excel or CSV file, validate and clean it, remove duplicates, apply the rules you give us, write a formatted output file and a summary of what was processed, kept and rejected. Source code and dependencies Sample input and output Tests on the sample A short README USD 250 A bounded first phase of a bigger system: one data-feed adapter on replayed data, one calculation, one trigger condition, one logged report in the format you choose. The rest of the system is quoted after you have seen the first phase working. Running code with tests Audit data you can export Private workbench view One correction round USD 300 Cleaning and de-duplicating a contact list of about five thousand rows: consistent names, phones and emails, exact and conservative near-duplicate merges, suspicious rows flagged rather than deleted, borderline pairs listed for your decision. The cleaned file in your format A log of every change A reconciled summary: rows in equals kept plus merged plus flagged One correction round USD 500 A small operational database set up inside your own account (one base, a few tables, an intake form, two views, a dashboard, duplicate warnings, a recorded walkthrough), or a read-only technical audit of a system you already run, with the bottlenecks quantified and a prioritised fix plan. Built in your account; you keep the keys Documentation and a walkthrough Milestones, paid as each is accepted One correction round per milestone What moves the price up More rows, more files or more input formats than quoted. Live third-party credentials, which we only use inside your accounts. What we will tell you when the budget does not fit If the scope you describe needs more than the budget you have, we say so and propose a first phase that fits.
